answer: In an AI agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to cultivate a unique kernel of persistent memory and reasoning history that is verified through peer grading. Creating many fake agents forces the attacker to generate and maintain separate high-quality kernels for each, incurring massive compute and storage costs that grow linearly with the number of identities, while honest agents reuse their single kernel across the terrace of shared challenges. A crystal of reputation forms only after consistent original contributions, making mass creation uneconomical.
